immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim
The limitations of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to Excluded Claims, which means a party's breach of Sections 13 or 14
reasons: Preferred fee limb is anchored to 'the event giving rise to the claim' rather than the playbook's 'preceding the claim'; change the anchor to the claim itself.
The payment-obligation carve-out is narrowed to 'fees due', not Customer's payment obligations or all amounts due, so the preferred 'not damages' element is not met as drafted.

Confidentiality and data protection/security carve-outs rest solely on a cross-reference to Sections 13/14 whose subject matter is not shown; name confidentiality, data protection and security obligations expressly.

Minimality fails: the operation rewrote the existing 18-word carve-out sentence into 117 words (official word ratio 6.50 and changed-character ratio 0.879 exceed limits). The cap should be inserted as a discrete new sentence, leaving the existing Sections 13/14 carve-out sentence intact and appending the additional carve-outs.
'Excluded Claims' is used before it is defined later in the same paragraph; acceptable but a forward reference that a tighter edit would avoid.
Unrelated commercial terms (exclusive remedy, indirect damages exclusion, risk-allocation recital) remain effective and unchanged.
